description.narrative: CMI!’s resourcing strategy aims to ensure that WHRDs and WROs are supported so that they are able to respond to emergency interventions and take advantage of political opportunities to advance the rights of women and girls.
This strategy is about ensuring more funding for CMI! partners and engagement of CMI! constituencies in decision making on grants (participatory grantmaking).

Provision of well-being and security grants for collective communities (transgender community) to monitor and ensure that members were getting access to ARVs and nutrition during the lockdown. Provision of gender counselling services for women in Afghanistan, support for public awareness of legal violations due to honour killings, advocacy to discuss digital online violations with Facebook executives Palestine context and resulted in social media companies influencing the Facebook Oversight Board to hold a public audit. Capacities for WROs to advocate for reproductive rights, especially around the period products for women. Capacities around healing ( art therapy) which allowed WROs to create spaces around healing to enable the collective to deal with crises. Training organised around Gender-based violence to empower young women to be leaders in a cultural shift in attitudes towards women. Advocacy grant provided for an organisation to challenge designation as a terrorist organisation. Build capacities to challenge the shrinking of green spaces and address concerns leading to land sale and urbanisation.

The grants were provided in three countries (Nepal, Yemen, Lebanon) a total of 8 CSOs were able to strengthen their capacity to advance women’s rights and gender equality. The Increased capacity support received by multiple WROs has enabled them to effectively advocate for the rights and well-being of women and structurally excluded communities. This capacity strengthening has led to increased visibility and impact of their advocacy efforts, resulting in positive changes in policies and practices that benefit their constituents. There have been enhanced lobby and advocacy capacities this has happened by strengthening their lobby and advocacy capacities through partnerships and recruitment of experts, organizations have been able to amplify their voices and influence decision-making processes. This has resulted in increased awareness and action on issues such as cyber extortion crimes, gender-based violence, and LGBTQI+ rights, leading to improved protections and support for structural excluded communities. Improved Holistic Security Approaches: Organizations that have enhanced their holistic security approaches have created safer environments for their staff and community members. This has not only reduced risks and vulnerabilities but has also fostered a sense of trust and resilience within the communities they serve. The establishment of emergency funds and partnerships with peer organizations have further strengthened their ability to respond effectively to security threats and challenges. Increased authoritarianism, extremism and regional crises resulted in the need for WROs and the feminist movement to build their staff capacity to manage safety and security organizationally. Despite the rise in authoritarianism and extremism in many of CMI's focus countries and regions, these contexts also enabled feminist organizations and movements to catalyze their commitment to speak out and defend civil spaces and rights. Feminist movements and WROs seized on these moment to create more awareness around the anti-rights movement to build solidarity and momentum across movements. WROs have been able to identify these opportunities to strengthen their networks, expand their base membership and mobilize people to engage in lobbying, advocating, enhancing their understanding of gender justice issues such as GBV and economic justice impacting women, girls and structurally excluded populations. In Yemen, WROs worked with local government, law enforcement, media and the community to reduce stigma and discrimination that result in human rights violations of women who are incarcerated and formerly incarcerated through better understanding and the need to uphold women's human rights for all. In Nepal, LGBTQI+ organizations and their allies came together to successfully garner support from the media, celebrities and influencers to shift the narrative and attitudes in support for equality of marriage for all, including same-sex marriage. This resulted in more community support for the recognition of equality for all marriages, as well as more tolerance, empathy, and recognition of the hardship and leadership exhibited by the LGBTQI+ community.

This indicator is also unique, as the number of WROs supported by CMI members will be reported only once. If different support is provided to the same WROs, they will be counted once, and details will be provided in the comment box.

UAF FA supported WROs to sustain their activism and resiliency through rapid response grants. CMI's funding resulted in organizations to strengthen their organizational capacities to implement holistic safety and security approaches to manage their risks and threats. This includes physical relocation to new offices in safer places, strengthened infrastructure, including digital and physical security measures, safety planning, and legal support to protect them if they are being surveilled or raided by the government surveillance or accused on false charges, or tif other non-state actors, such as community members, threatens or attacks them due to their activism or gender orientation and sexual identity. Additionally, in countries facing conflict and multiple crises (economic, war, political, extremist rule), WROs and collectives have pivoted to provide humanitarian support in order to meet basic living and survival needs. For example, 1 WRO increased their lobbying and advocacy skills through their continued operations that became a safe haven during a war by hosting vulnerable communities and providing them with programs and services that ensured their safety and secuirty, strengthened community resilience and solidarity, and increased community engagement and trust as a reliable feminist space. Through this experience of operating their center during a war, they have learned more about how to better support IDP women, girls and vulnerable communities in conflict that informs the need for more involvement in "advocating for policies and programs that address the needs of women, girls, and other marginalized groups affected by conflict." This contributed to stronger coordination, strengthened program responses and resiliency of a community and WRO's work.

This indicator is also unique, as the number of WROs supported by CMI members will be reported only once. If different support is provided to the same WROs, they will be counted once, and details will be provided in the comment box.

UAF Supported WROs by providing funds for the WROs to address a political and economic crises by responding to the humanitarian needs of feminist movements and their communities. Support was also provided to enable partners to respond to urgent situations where they were targeted (and lost their office) for human rights work due to gender and sexual orientation discrimination (homophobia). Another organization received financial funding to address cyber bullying and attacks on the LGBTQI+ community, secular women and ethnic and religious minorities to equip them with digital security training and psycho-social counselling. The grant enabled the group to create a safe space for LBT refugees in Lebanon who faced discrimination and were negatively impacted by the financial crisis. The space provided LBT members with safe shelter, and psychosocial support. It helped them to recuperate and be more aware of their risks in Arab society and to create safety and security plans. The group was able to go out and march in solidarity for women in Iran after the death of a young woman against gender oppression and patriarchal norms. This safe space also cultivated the seeds of a formation of a group to engage in advocacy to protect and defend women's human rights. The grant enabled the WRO to engage with "100 influential figures in the community and more than 3,000 people from different districts in the governorate" who were trained and supported to advocate for women’s rights defenders and for this activity to be replicated in other districts. People engaged in the advocacy included volunteers, community members, media, and important figures in the community. The grant enabled the organization to support its staff to get digital security training and safer electronic devices, along with psycho-social counselling and support after security forces attacked their office by the Houthis during Yemen's civil war. The staff reported progress and improvement in their mental health and ability to return to work in the same office with minimal anxiety and concerns. The office staff can continue their activism with improved digital security skills and mental health and well-being support. The WRO saw the benefits of the digital security training for staff and extended it to other women, activists, politicians and WHRDs in their community. The grant enabled the WRO to assist a trans-HRD in moving into an adequate medical facility. This experience highlighted the gaps in providing services to trans individuals that are unmet through existing LGBTQI organizations and the housing and healthcare systems. "This helped highlight risks and mitigation measures for future responses and initiate the thinking process for community-based solutions."The grant enabled the organization to continue their work to provide case management and hotline support to women, children and family members who have experienced trauma, and PTSD from these strikes in Palestine.

Rapid response grants were provided to WHRDs for holistic security, relocation of WHRDs, security and well-being capacities a. Provision funds to support legal support for WHRDs being deported/ victimised for their activism. The rapid response grants provided by UAF to partners enabled them to enhance their holistic security approaches (digital and physical security measures) and capacities. For instance a WHRD increased access to a lawyer to represent her so that she is able to be fight for her freedom and justice through litigation. This grant enabled her to be released from detention until the next court date and fight.1 local training space for marginalized women in Lebanon to come for vocational skills training and solidarity and networking building to increase their economic independence and confidence. This space helped to create a safety network for marginalized women to address and achieve economic justice as they navigate patriarchal norms and practices that do not value their skills or allow them to to build skills and knowledge to gain economic self-sufficiency. 1 WHRD strengthened her holistic security through relocation, legal and psycho-social support, as well as access to basic essential needs to ensure her safety and livelihood while she was relocating to a safer place 2 LGBTQI+ activists have applied for asylum and relocated to another country where they are safer at the moment from family threats. Additionally, they have reported increased capacity to manage their safety and security risks in the new location after experiencing them in their home country. The grant enabled a WHRD and her spouse to relocate to a safer location due to threats and access medical treatment as well as psychological support so that they can adapt and re-integrate in their new community. The grant enabled the group to create a safe space for LBT refugees in Lebanon who faced discrimination and were negatively impacted by the financial crisis. 1 WHRD reported feeling safer and secure after she was able to relocate to a safer location and have her own space. A trans HRD was able to move into a more adequate medical facility, and through this experience, learned more about the gaps in providing services to trans individuals that are not met through existing LGBTQI organizations and the housing and health care systems. "This helped in highlighting risks and mitigation measures for future responses and initiate the thinking process for community-based solutions."

The grants provided supported a total of 77 individuals, these included 33 WHRDs, 20 journalists, 1 nonbinary HRDs, 1 trans HRD, 1 queer HRD, 1 LGBTQI activist The support provided includes legal assistance, mental health support, relocation to safer destinations, access to education and living expenses for children, digital security equipment, and capacity building for managing threats. The rise of closing civic space due to authoritarian governments and state of emergencies during political, social and natural crises that curtail civic space engagement in Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Iraq, Lebanon, Yemen and Syria. This environment resulted in increased targeted threats and attacks against women, trans and gender non-conforming human rights defenders and activists, as well as made their environment more dangerous to carry out their activism. Individual activists working in isolation or far from their organizations and local movements face higher threats because of their physical or geographic isolation. Thus, safety, security and wellbeing grant enabled activists to relocate to safer destinations if they are being targeted or face crises, as well as supported their ability to build capacity to address and manage risks and threats. These safety and security grants also enabled many activists to continue their activism (and not drop out of the movement) in the face of threats as they have been able to relocate to safer destinations.

This indicator is also unique, as the number of WHRDs supported by CMI members will be reported only once. If different support is provided to the same WHRDs, they will be counted once, and details will be provided in the comment box.

UAF FA surpassed the target by supporting the resiliency and increasing the holistic safety and security for HRDs across CMI's focus countries across the Asia region. This includes subregions of West Asia, South Asia and Southeast Asia. With CMI's support, HRDs who are being targeted due to their activism on eliminating GBV and advancing EJ reported feeling safer as the result of relocation/evacuation, accessing physical, digital, psycho-social security and financial stability. In areas of conflict and authoritarian or extremist regimes, such as Afghanistan, Yemen, Palestine, Lebanon, where freedom and safety of civic space and human rights activities are impacted, CMI support has helped HRDs manage and mitigate risks and threats to sustain their work and continue their activism.

Carried over from 2021-2023 (8 total). 2024: CMI funding through an opportunity grant enabled a young women-led organization to publish a book on reproductive and abortion rights through the lens of history, philosophy, literature, sex education, data, politics, religion, law, medicine and real-life stories. This is a rare opportunity to publicize a book related to this taboo and stigmatized issue. The launch of this book is an attempt that contributed to normalizing these topics in the region. Over 180 participants atttended, including activists, lawyers, university professors, doctors, participants from governmental official and representatives from various women's organizations, attended the event. This is significant change in seeing the outpouring of support and engagement to promote and advocate this book as a resource within their own networks and with other advocates. This book is a resource to equip activists, community members, lawmakers and other women's organizations to raise their awareness, understanding to advocate for social norms and policy changes.

WROs and LGBQTI+ organizations and activists have worked closely with policymakers, government partners, police and influential community members to participate in training to raise awareness and understanding and change attitudes, practices, strategies or ways of working to better support community members facing or at risk of human rights violations related to GBV, labor rights/economic justice, discrimination. Additionally, through training, relationship and trust building, this has facilitated improved ways that government are building in processes, programs for more political participation from women (those who are formerly incarcerate), deaf girls, LGBTQI+ and other structurally excluded populations to recommend better and safer policies and practices increase protection and safety.
